findings.title: Repository requests can supply executable sensor commands
findings.description: Validation allowlists each sensor ID but copies its entire Configuration dictionary without validating permitted keys or values. This unit demonstrates that `command` is an executable sensor configuration setting for ESLint. Consequently, a repository-registration request can replace that server-generated command with attacker-controlled text, crossing from configuration data into an execution-bearing channel. Any sensor runner that honors the stored command will execute authority supplied by the request rather than by trusted server configuration.
findings.recommendation: Define a strict, typed schema for every sensor and reject unknown keys. Do not accept command lines, executable paths, arguments, report paths, or working directories directly from repository-registration requests; construct them from trusted server-side definitions. If customization is required, allowlist individual safe options and validate paths under the registered repository before execution.

findings.title: Validated repository paths can be replaced before use
findings.description: Root paths are checked for allowed-root containment and reparse traversal only when loaded or registered. `Access` later passes the stored path directly to `RepositoryAccess` without revalidating it. A filesystem actor able to rename the validated directory or one of its ancestors and replace it with a symbolic link or junction after validation can redirect subsequent access outside the configured roots.
findings.recommendation: Revalidate containment and reparse traversal immediately before creating each RepositoryAccess, and ensure RepositoryAccess applies equivalent checks to every resolved target. For stronger protection against rename races, anchor operations to directory handles or otherwise verify the canonical target at the actual filesystem operation rather than relying only on a previously validated path string.

findings.title: Unbounded registration data can exhaust memory and registry storage
findings.description: DisplayName and every sensor configuration key and value are accepted and persisted without length or aggregate-size limits. A caller able to create or update registrations can submit very large strings or dictionaries, forcing allocation during copying and serialization and permanently enlarging the registry read at startup. The sensor count is bounded indirectly, but each sensor's dictionary is not.
findings.recommendation: Apply explicit limits to display-name length, configuration entry count, key length, value length, and the aggregate serialized registration size. Also enforce an appropriately small request-body limit at the API boundary and reject oversized data before copying or persistence.
